rationale: B is better structured and more technically discriminating, especially in separating full engines from renderers and distinguishing Babylon.js from Three.js; A incorrectly groups them and claims both require building physics, input, and scene management yourself. B also adds the useful PixiJS option and gives clearer recommendations by use case. It is not flawless—the claim that melonJS is built on LimeJS appears incorrect, and its blanket advice to avoid Unity WebGL is too strong—but overall its comparisons are more accurate, actionable, and calibrated.
